Orda Aldresia (A77)

Survey-table region: Anbennar Empire (EoA).

In a sentence: Guard the Empire with magic, gunblades, and knightly vows—but decide whether the Emperor, the people, or the faith comes first.

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 80/100 | Autocracy 75/100 | Magic–Artifice 50/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 92/100) | Pluralism 55/100. Phase shift: restoration of the guardian's mission (Autocracy 55) → coercive political route (Autocracy 82).

The v2.1 values assessment is Neutral (55/100), with a branch-dependent trajectory. Phase values: protection and reconstruction (Good, 78/100) → the Second Son's coercive political route (Neutral, 45/100).

Story: High | Mission-tree length: Medium (19 exclusive missions, with a conditional later tree change) | Mission-tree version: base Mod v1.37.5.0; content discussed in official diaries from 2024–2025 | Distinctiveness: Very high | Tedium: High | Early pressure: Medium-high | Expansion: Medium-high.

Why the Imperial Guard lost its reputation

In 1444, Orda Aldresia is a Regent Court theocracy using a secular-knightly order reform. It has its own culture, capital, and Grandmaster, as well as a mage organisation and commanders divided into factions; the historical record places it with the Lilac War's Moon Party. This is no ordinary county: imperial duties, special political relationships, and its own military tradition jointly shape its position. 【Local history script】【Local Chinese localisation】

The offline English Wiki traces the organisation's origins to the Aldresian Crusade and the arcane-knight tradition created to protect the Emperor of Anbennar. Its knights' art of casting spells through their swords came through elven transmission; their duty to guard the throne also made them long-standing rivals of the Magisterium. This background explains why guns, swords, magic, and the imperial court appear together rather than as unrelated themes. 【Wiki】

When the Greentide invaded in 1424, young knights wanted to fight in Escann, but senior leaders forbade intervention because of the Empire's civil war. Some members left and formed adventuring companies. The Order's sharpest historical conflict had already emerged before the campaign began: did its vow to protect the Empire permit it to ignore suffering on the Empire's frontier? The Wiki's later account of a Grandmaster's assassination, a religious turn, and expeditions belongs to post-opening setting narrative; it must not all be written as reforms already completed by 1444. 【Wiki】

Reforging the Imperial Guard

The 19 national missions begin with postwar reconstruction and restoring the Order's reputation. The arsenal requires production, commercial influence, and investment in buildings. The archive recruits scholars and engineers, then uses iron, mage towers, and cannon to advance the combination of firearms, magic, and steel. The knights' development is not merely another army bonus: it changes how equipment and organisation support their imperial duty. 【Local script】【Local narrative text】

The Grand Vault and precursor relics make the route more dangerous. The country invests in a relic system and uses hybrid magic and sacred gunblades; the text also proposes collecting dark objects to fight the Magisterium. This is a political vision of “using dangerous tools to protect the community.” The relics' danger alone does not make the route evil: the relevant question is whom they ultimately protect or harm. 【Local script】【Local narrative text】

Returning to the imperial court requires the Emperor, allies, and a military presence. The missions emphasise loyalty to Anbennar, not to a particular ruler. Yet this self-image can also give the Order grounds to interfere in imperial domestic affairs. Reputation, alliances, and freedom of action constrain one another, so a strong military does not mean the opening is free to conquer at will. 【Local script】【Local narrative text】

A protector may become a usurper

Investigating Ashniande's murder and kidnapping, entering the cursed forest, and pursuing Corvurian shadow forces all lead toward the duty to protect people who cannot protect themselves. The route to winning public support explicitly promises bread, safety, and prosperity: the Order does not serve only noble duelists. Public protection and military-political power are two sides of the same institution. 【Local narrative text】

Another set of events, however, allows the Order to restructure an occupied country under the “Second Son” order: kill the local ruler and heir, install a replacement, and impose vassalage. This is not merely warfare or monarchy, but the deliberate taking of lives and political coercion. A narrative justification in terms of opposing corruption or restoring order does not erase the means used. 【Local script】

The current national missions also include a Ravelian religious route. Specific events and choices can allow the Order to inherit a related country, become the Ravelian Curia's subject (Z97), and switch to a non-generic mission tree. This is not an automatic addition of another A77 mission file, and not every player is renamed. The full mechanics of the new Tag's ending are not covered here; community descriptions of a radical late game should not be applied unconditionally to every A77 opening. 【Local script】

Feel, values, and recommendation

First repair the arsenal, win support, and restore the Order's reputation. In the middle game, act amid imperial politics, the Magisterium, and shadow forces while developing gunblades and relics. Only later do you decide how to handle religious and political power. Waiting, support requirements, technology and buildings, and special relationships are the main sources of tedium. Two player accounts disagree about narrative continuity: one enjoys the multi-stage turns, while another finds the later jump too abrupt. They document a real difference of opinion, not one correct route. 【Community opinion】

The provisional personality is Expansion 80 / Autocracy 75 / Magic–Artifice direction 50 (intensity 92) / Pluralism 55; the overall values assessment is Neutral 55 and depends chiefly on the branch. Protecting civilians, relief, and rebuilding the arsenal are positive evidence. Killing an occupied ruler and heir and installing a puppet significantly reduce dignity and restraint. The phase assessment moves from protector toward coercive politics; militarisation or religious change alone is not treated as wrongdoing.

Recommended for players who enjoy imperial politics, a magical military order, and the risk of guardians becoming oppressors. If you want complete independence from the start, a linear mission tree, or only a bright chivalric fairy tale, choose another country. See the evidence page for sources and the conditional successor.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Orda Aldresia (A77) — Aldresian Ideas

Set ID: A77_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = A77
    }

Aldresian Traditions

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

  • global_spy_defence：+20% (global_spy_defence; raw value 0.2).

1. Knights Sworn to the Empire

“Hear my vows, Castellos, King of Gods and God of Kings, and bind me to my words as law, O lawgiver. I shall hold no lands, accept no titles, take no partner and bear no children. I shall be just and true, fair and vigilant, valiant and ardent. With your wisdom, make me an unbreakable shield, a shining sword, an indomitable fortress protecting and being guided by the dream of Anbennar. Give me the strength to fight eternal against the forces of darkness, that till my sword breaks and my light extinguishes, I can stand tall as a true Knight of Aldresia.”" With these words is one inducted into the hallowed ranks of the order. Such vows are not taken lightly and this becomes reflected in the devotion members show to their duties.

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

2. Imperial Mediators

The Grandmaster of the Orda Aldresia has the distinguished privilege of acting as imperial proxy during times of peace. Beyond mediating disputes between conflicting parties within the empire, the Grandmaster also ensures imperial edicts are followed and that the rights of the various estates are being respected. This great responsibility affords the order significant sway in attracting talented aides.

  • Diplomats: +1 (diplomats; raw value 1).

3. Arcane Knights

The Orda Aldresia is one of the only remaining organizations that utilizes the lost art of Diranbe. Formal induction into the order requires that novitiates master the difficult task of utilizing a spellblade as their focus while engaging in melee combat. Those who are able to achieve such an undertaking are accepted and become one of the fabled arcane knights. The devastating charge of the arcane knights single handedly won many fields for the nobles during the brutal Wars of Rule.

  • Shock damage: +10% (shock_damage; raw value 0.1).

4. The Aldresian Crusade

In 1053 AA, our namesake Aldresia, led a crusade against the undead hordes and ended the White Pestilence. Aldresia and her followers were instrumental in halting one of the worst abuses wrought by magic in all of Cannorian history, thus ensuring our order remains highly respected even until this day.

  • Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1).

5. The Anbenncóst Accords

The conclusion of the Wars of Rule saw the Anbennarian magocracy ousted and the nobles install Marion of the House Silmuna as Emperor. For the orders loyal service during the wars, Emperor Marion I granted the order extensive land in the eastern border territories along with the rights of imperial immediacy. This distinct right ensures that the order is exempt from paying taxes or fealty to any lord but the Emperor, thus greatly increasing our ability to raise funds and fill the coffers of Arca Aldresia.

  • National tax modifier: +10% (global_tax_modifier; raw value 0.1).

6. Institution of Martial Magecraft

Our privileged status as one of two sanctioned magical bodies within Anbennar affords us great prestige. This coupled with the strong military traditions of the Order ensures that we are never short of recruits from those magic users more interested in the martial applications of their gifts. Even the order's greenest recruits are able to hold their own in the field of battle under the direction of the order's masters.

  • Army tradition: +1 (army_tradition; raw value 1).

  • Manpower recovery speed: +15% (manpower_recovery_speed; raw value 0.15).

7. Bastion of the Order

Arca Aldresia stands as a testament to the resolve and tenacity of the order. Built atop the ruins of Rotwall to commemorate the conclusion of the decades long Aldresian Crusade with the aid of the greatest abjurers and military minds of the day, the castle has evolved over the centuries into one of the most formidable fortresses in all of Anbennar.

This great citadel was able to withstand even the might of the magisters who attempted to siege it at the climax of the Wars of Rule. The humiliating defeat of the magocrats ensured continued animosity between the order and the Magisterium. Even with the advent of blackpowder, the Arca Aldresia remains nigh impregnable thanks to its multitude of magical defences and the diligence of the orders knights.

  • Fort defense: +25% (defensiveness; raw value 0.25).

Ravelian State (Z97) — Ravelian Ideas

Set ID: Z97_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = Z97
    }

Ravelian Traditions

  • Technology cost: -10% (technology_cost; raw value -0.1).

  • Religious unity: +25% (religious_unity; raw value 0.25).

1. Universal Revelations to the Truth

The Ravelian Church can only be rivalled by the Jadd in their mission to spread the faith to all corners of the world. As each Revelation is discovered (a major finding unearthed or doctrine settled within the church), the closer the faith gets to the Truth (a total understanding of the world), and the more the faith must spread bring the world to the fold.

Once the world is converted to the true faith, the Ravelians believe that God will be empowered once more and grant salvation to all.

  • Prestige per development from conversion: +0.3 (prestige_per_development_from_conversion; raw value 0.3).

2. Ravelian Society Origins

The Ravelian Church was born from the Ravelian Society, a group of academics and reformists that wished to unravel the secrets of the world through reason and empiricism. The first members of the society were in fact Corinites who were unconvinced that fighting injustice with sword and shield was enough, and sought for a greater fight against lies and injustice that would encompass the whole world, not just Cannor.

The Ravelian Society eventually became a place for great thinkers in a time when religious conflict and superstition was rife, and to this day their legacy of reason still permeates through the church.

  • Advisor cost: -10% (advisor_cost; raw value -0.1).

3. Aspects of the One God

The Ravelian belief in a One God is quite unique in the world of Halann. While most other faiths are polytheistic, and even the faith of Surael accepts the existence of other gods (while claiming they are dead), the Ravelian Church is truly monotheistic, believing that there is only one god. The Ravelian One God is seen as all-knowing, all-powerful and all-present - all other gods are either aspects of (a part of) God, saints that emulate God's ideal, or non-existent and false.

  • Maximum Absolutism: +10 (max_absolutism; raw value 10).

4. Warrior Automata

A type of Mechanim created by the church to serve as soldiers, guards and holy warriors. The first automata stood well above the common man, and were armed with large tower shields capable of defending their charge, in addition to an embedded gun in the other arm to fend off the unholy. Since then the Warrior Automata have become a feared reminder of what happens when religious zeal and intellectual brilliance is combined.

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

5. Original Sin of the Precursor Elves

"It is said that God created all things, and would bestow magic, their own power, to their creations when they deemed them worthy. The precursor elves, one of their creations, were not worthy. And so in their envy and impatience, conspired with each other to strike down God and steal their power for themselves.

But lo, they could not defeat God truly, for God was all-powerful. They could not find God, for God was all-present everywhere. They could not deceive God, for God was all-knowing.

But in God's wisdom they allowed themselves to be deceived by their plot and defeated by their creations, and bound into the God Fragment. For God has compassion and empathy for their creation, and knew that one day they may prove themselves truly worthy and redeem themselves in the eyes of the Lord."

-Provenance 1:23-30

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

6. Artificer-Priests

The Ravelian Society, and later the church, were responsible for many great advancements in the field of artificery. The Church believed that magic was divine, and that artificery was a way to allow all of God's creations to benefit from Their power (magic).

Many Rectors (the common name for a priest) were knowledgable in the art of artificery, and one of their main responsibilities was tending to the needs of the faithful, which in this case not only involved traditional religious duties, but also acting as teachers and mentors, but also as local artificers creating and repairing inventions for the needy.

  • National unrest: -1 (global_unrest; raw value -1).

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

7. Speaker for the God Fragment

Said to be the last vessel of a defeated One True God, the God Fragment is guarded in a hidden location only known to the upper echelons of the High Rectorate. The God Fragment is monitored for its rare communications, which it does through high-pitched frequencies that can be deciphered and translated into an variant of precursor elven. The High Rector and the Veridicals are the first to hear the messages of the God Fragment, and it is often up to them to discern what revelations and insights it can offer - once a new revelation is found, the High Rector acts as the speaker to evocate the God Fragment's message.

  • All power costs: -5% (all_power_cost; raw value -0.05).

Ravelian Ambition

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).
